justifications.durability: the fix makes the fakes return the shape the owner's query actually yields, so the drop branch is exercised rather than short-circuited, and the negative control demonstrates the drop assertions fail if the drop is removed; the streaming tests now also assert the owner's index-setup call is made exactly once (client.index_ensures == 1). The guard is therefore shown to fire, not merely green.
justifications.evidence: the reviewed run carries a reproducing baseline (baseline.log: 4 failed, 5 passed, EXIT=1) matching the plan's four named failures — two _FakeClient AttributeError from the missing ensure_vector_indexes, two TestDimensionMismatchDetection drops short-circuited by a KeyError on 'props' (client.py:485 logs "Could not check vector index shape: 'props'") — plus a committed-head gate (final-head.log: 9 passed, EXIT=0) and a mutation control (negative-control.log: 2 failed, EXIT=1). I independently re-ran the two files at abb02d6a0 (repro-head.log: 9 passed, EXIT=0) and re-derived the negative control in a scratch extraction by setting dimension_differs=False (scratch-nc.log: 2 failed, EXIT=1), so the drop guard fires exactly as declared.
justifications.fit: the commit subject 'test(graph): align vector index fakes with client interface' carries a body stating what changed and why; the added symbols (index_ensures, props) describe the mechanism; no plan, sprint, ticket or phase identifier appears in the diff, message or comments.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §53 asks that the dimension-mismatch drop and the streaming tests be restored against the single owner GraphClient.ensure_vector_indexes, repairing production code where the refactor lost the drop behaviour and the test doubles where only they lag the new interface. The commit touches only the two test files: both fakes gain the interface the owner exposes (imas_codex/graph/client.py:407, called from imas_codex/graph/dd_identifier_enrichment.py:354 and imas_codex/graph/dd_ids_enrichment.py:455), and the fake index rows gain the `props` field the owner's SHOW INDEXES query returns. The drop behaviour was intact at the base — ensure_vector_indexes still drops an owned index whose dimension differs (client.py:446-483) — so no production repair was warranted and none was made. Both files pass at the head and the negative control fails the two drop tests, meeting both done-when clauses.
justifications.reuse: the change extends the existing _FakeClient and the existing TestDimensionMismatchDetection fixtures and keeps GraphClient.ensure_vector_indexes as the single index-DDL owner; no parallel index path or duplicate DDL was introduced.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat abb02d6a0 lists exactly tests/graph/test_dd_aux_streaming.py and tests/graph/test_vector_quantization.py — the two paths the manifest declares in changed_paths. No production file is touched and no second index-DDL path is added, matching the plan's constraint. client.py was named in orientation_write_paths but correctly left unchanged once the defect was localised to the doubles.
